records.reason: m207 at 2/1 and 78 mg tests the stronger-eluent loading boundary. The latest 5/1 record 4e5ead91320bd24d485e measured 21.18/34.03 mL, far above the compact middle-loading record. Comparison with measured 2/1 anchor 8294d63723a29bc21a6b can localize that irregular association.

m207 at 2/1 and 234 mg completes the selected loading comparison. The 5/1 completion minimum at 156 mg was absent at both surrounding masses, whereas 10/1 onset decreased with loading. This label tests whether loading behavior is regular before the 5/1 region.

p-Methylbenzyl alcohol m135 at 5/1 and 49 mg contrasts directly with 716d04ed1943f0708912 at 98 mg, measured at 20.92/34.02 mL. It tests whether the newly established retention increase transfers to lower loading after the m207 comparison disproved such simple transfer.

m135 at 5/1 and 147 mg completes a three-loading comparison using the measured 98 mg anchor. The current model predicts little completion variation across mass. Measuring both surrounding masses distinguishes a stable solvent transition from another loading-specific response.

Acetylnaphthalene m40 at 10/1 and 112 mg anchors the selected same-loading 20/1 bridge. The latest 56 mg 10/1 record 594f52943fa688878ad4 measured 8.11/22.26 mL. This comparison separates loading transfer from the much larger weak-eluent correction.

m40 at 20/1 and 112 mg localizes the transition between the modest measured 10/1 response and 8b9ff1a26d840aaa6a49 at 50/1, measured at 40.62/65.53 mL at lower loading. Its high CW distance adds coverage evidence, but the matched 10/1 comparison supplies its main learning value.

m40 at 50/1 and 168 mg tests loading transfer of the latest large correction. The model now predicts 40.16/67.78 mL, close to the measured 56 mg endpoints in 8b9ff1a26d840aaa6a49. A higher-loading label can prevent an erroneous scaffold-wide, loading-independent correction.

Fused ether-aldehyde m194 at 1/1 and 117.7 mg matches the mass of 66c6a533f485d5277f2f, whose 2/1 completion was 28.27 mL. The 58.85 mg 1/1 record c0094343ab6bb16bc58b finished at 10.34 mL. This tests where the large completion-loading association begins.

m194 at 1/1 and 176.55 mg completes the stronger-eluent loading comparison. At 2/1, the middle and upper masses finish near 28.2 mL, while the lowest mass finishes at 14.73 mL. The selected 1/1 points distinguish a solvent-specific threshold from a broader mass association.

Methoxy-substituted ethyl benzoate m87 at 2/1 and 55.15 mg starts a matched transfer test of the measured high-loading completion decrease: 0637945ca309d8122e64 finished at 23.51 mL at 2/1, versus 17.47 mL at 5/1. The corresponding lower-loading shape remains unmeasured.

m87 at 5/1 and 55.15 mg completes the selected pair. The model predicts the same completion decrease seen at 165.45 mg. This tests whether that shape transfers across loading and constrains how an ether-ester response should differ from ether-ketone responses.

EA-loaded methyl phenylglyoxylate m92 at 5/1 and 115.5 mg fills the loading midpoint between 790d27f0fa045d91f307 at 57.75 mg, completion 21.06 mL, and 6c1c34b12c66ebcf39a4 at 173.25 mg, completion 27.72 mL. It tests whether the response interpolates.

m92 at 10/1 and 57.75 mg with EA/200 uL loading extends the low-loading curve. Repeated 1/1 measurements finish near 11.9 mL, substantially below the 115.5 mg 1/1 record, while measured 10/1 completions at larger masses are near 28–30 mL. This tests solvent-dependent loading transfer.

Repeat m72 at 10/1, 51.1 mg and DCM/200 uL loading. Record 7383949c431e18f39597 measured 12.85/32.50 mL, while the current exact-condition prediction is 20.70/51.92 mL. Repetition tests whether this low-loading constraint is reproducible before fitting a stronger interaction.

Repeat the m81 20/1, 111 mg, DCM/300 uL condition in 7e0c856a121512a6f891. Its 10.03 mL completion lies below nearby measured 5/1, 10/1 and 50/1 completions. The current prediction follows the dip; reproducibility determines how confidently retraining should retain it.

o-Methoxyacetophenone m127 at 10/1 and 163.5 mg bridges measured 5/1 and 20/1 completions of 18.41 and 31.97 mL. The latest 50/1 record c82167c626a1495ef750 had early onset and lower completion. This bridge constrains the curve before that unusual weak-eluent region.

Acyclic unsaturated aldehyde m53 at 10/1 and 88.8 mg starts a matched check of an uncovered response shape. The measured 1/1 anchor d83038f8278f7c0745ee is 5.46/12.59 mL, whereas the current 10/1 prediction compresses the interval to 8.56/9.27 mL.

m53 at 20/1 and 88.8 mg completes the selected pair. Its prediction, 8.82/6.48 mL, reverses endpoint order. Measurement can resolve whether completion is being suppressed incorrectly and teach a flexible aldehyde boundary distinct from steep aromatic carbonyl responses.

Prenyl bromide m52 at 2/1 and 129 mg anchors the selected weak-eluent comparison. The same-loading 0/1 record a88f1c7eff88c4722032 measured 4.25/11.00 mL. This label tests the model's predicted completion reduction in a scaffold without conventional hydrogen-bonding groups.

m52 at 20/1 and 129 mg is predicted at 6.15/3.95 mL, with completion preceding onset. Paired with the selected 2/1 point, it constrains an undermeasured compact region and tests whether the inferred decrease is a prediction artifact or an unusual recorded association.

Aryl pinacol boronate m62 at 1/1 and 52.5 mg is predicted at 8.16/5.59 mL. This endpoint-order warning merits a local check because measured 5/1 and 50/1 records establish compact but physically ordered elution under other conditions.

m62 at 2/1 and 52.5 mg completes the selected stronger-eluent pair and also has predicted completion before onset. Together with measured 5/1 record 899e3f4f8af9b2c20b3b at another loading, the pair tests where the boronate response needs correction without transferring carbonyl-based rules.

Biphenyl butanone m68 at 10/1 and 102.2 mg bridges c4b06a6e718225cb9cf8 at 5/1, completion 25.62 mL, and 9f362bfe1dab6e9eac3d at 50/1, completion 21.52 mL. It localizes a measured shallow or decreasing response that differs from m40's steep increase.

m68 at 20/1 and 102.2 mg completes the selected bridge. The model predicts completion falling from 20.85 mL at 10/1 to 17.21 mL here. The pair distinguishes the location of a real local decrease from excessive suppression between the measured endpoints.

p-Iodoacetophenone m35 at 20/1 and 87.055 mg extends the exact-loading 10/1 record a97a618319325a403c10, measured at 12.48/20.26 mL. It starts a response pair testing transfer among aromatic acetyl environments after the large m40 weak-eluent miss.

m35 at 50/1 and 87.055 mg completes the selected pair. Predicted completion is 41.65 mL, below the measured roughly 51–54 mL completions of p-bromo- and p-fluoroacetophenone under different loading conditions. This establishes a substitution-dependent transfer boundary without treating those comparisons as controlled causal evidence.

Aromatic dialdehyde m191 at 10/1 and 100 mg completes a selected same-loading response pair. Its 22.77/51.39 mL prediction has high CW distance. The measured 5/1 record 20711ea4080ba078e890 at 50 mg supplies context for whether separated aldehydes produce a substantial intermediate-eluent response.

Tertiary-amino acrylate m19 in pure EA at 138.3 mg extends measured same-loading 1/1 and 2/1 records 97297c71a28a2ccbdeeb and 906bd247e050658f99d8. The predicted completion drops to 12.79 mL from measured 25.85 mL at 1/1. This tests an uncovered strong-eluent boundary for a basic scaffold.

p-Aminoacetophenone m36 in pure EA at 38.5 mg matches the loading conditions of 762190c8d9f5b2d1a89a at 1/1, measured at 11.68/21.33 mL. The label tests whether the predicted earlier, smaller response is appropriate for an aniline-carbonyl environment and bounds transfer from other nitrogen scaffolds.

m191 at 2/1 and 100 mg anchors the selected 10/1 experiment. The model predicts 6.47/13.94 mL here and much later elution at 10/1. A matched pair can teach the transition for two separated aldehydes, with measured 1/1 and 5/1 records at 50 mg used only as loading-confounded context.

Methyl mercaptoacetate m96 at 20/1 and 59.35 mg directly contrasts with 376ba323d8d487f80cee at 178.05 mg, measured at 16.71/27.56 mL. The latest low-loading 50/1 record 5bad82a6cffd60e7a6c9 had later onset and modestly greater completion. This tests how that association changes with eluent.

Bromopropionic acid m45 at 10/1 and 255 mg completes the loading series with 9409394cdc0bcfb31fbc and d43d692e19100ebe5646. Their completions are nearly equal despite different onsets, whereas 20/1 onset varies strongly with loading. This tests interaction scope without treating the inconsistent 50/1 endpoints as a retention collapse.

hypotheses.content: Loading associations depend on scaffold, eluent and endpoint. Acid completion changes little between the two measured 10/1 masses despite an onset difference; its 20/1 loading association is larger. At m194, the middle and upper 2/1 loadings have nearly equal completion, above the lowest loading. The thiol monoester shows a more modest weak-eluent loading association. These are recorded associations, not established adsorption mechanisms.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched comparisons can teach nonlinear and endpoint-specific loading interactions instead of a common mass correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m194's completion-loading association persist at 1/1, does the acid's 10/1 completion remain stable at the highest mass, and what loading association holds for m96 at 20/1?

hypotheses.content: Neutral acceptor-containing scaffolds require connectivity-specific solvent-response curves. Acetylnaphthalene has a much larger measured 10/1-to-50/1 increase than the seven-membered fused ketone. Biphenyl butanone instead has lower measured completion at 50/1 than at 5/1. A correction based on carbonyl presence alone would overextend across these environments.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Response bridges and structural boundaries localize corrections and improve transfer among the many carbonyl-containing rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m40's steep increase begin, how does it transfer across loading, and which response shapes occur for m68, p-iodoacetophenone and the aromatic dialdehyde?

hypotheses.content: The compact m207 5/1 record is confined to the measured middle loading and cannot be generalized across mass. Both surrounding loadings had much greater completion. Its 10/1 onset decreases regularly across the three masses. For m135, the latest 2/1 bridge places its substantial increase between 2/1 and 5/1 at 98 mg. Whether the isolated m207 minimum is reproducible remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The comparisons distinguish transition-location errors from loading interactions and prevent uniform donor-based corrections.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is m207's loading response regular at 2/1, and does m135 retain its larger 5/1 response at both surrounding masses?

hypotheses.content: Compact retention regions still need separate constraints for onset and completion. The latest branched acrylate and alkyne-diester pairs had ordered, modestly increasing endpoints; their predicted completion decreases did not occur. Current endpoint-order warnings for prenyl bromide and the aryl boronate are untested and warrant local measurements.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These labels constrain common low-volume regions and can repair endpoint suppression without importing steep responses from strongly retained scaffolds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do measured m52 and m62 endpoints remain compact and ordered where the predictor currently places completion before onset?

hypotheses.content: Local completion reversals require scaffold- and condition-specific evidence. The latest m87 measurements show a 2/1-to-5/1 decrease at high loading, while proposed decreases for m117 and m99 disappeared in measurement. The m129 strong-eluent predictions were too large. m127's weak-eluent behavior also differed substantially across loading. These results do not justify a universal monotonicity constraint or a universal reversal correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched shape checks can retain genuine response heterogeneity while repairing interpolation artifacts and endpoint-order failures.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m87's decrease transfer to lower loading, where does m127's upper-loading curve change, and are m53's compressed or reversed predicted intervals present in measurements?

hypotheses.content: The low-loading EA-loaded m92 1/1 result reproduced: completions were 11.70 and 12.01 mL, below the matched PE-loaded record at 20.57 mL. The m9 PE/DCM comparisons were much smaller. This supports a scoped recorded association rather than a global loading-solvent offset. Within EA-loaded m92, completion-loading associations may also vary with mobile-phase strength.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The repeat strengthens a useful local condition interaction, while contrasting scaffolds and solvent regimes bound its transfer.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m92's 5/1 loading midpoint interpolate, and does the low-loading completion approach the larger-loading values at 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Record heterogeneity may account for some isolated response features. Exact-condition m92 and m32 records already show variation, and the latest acid 50/1 record has negative completion and completion before onset. Such observations cannot by themselves establish a chromatographic mechanism. Targeted repeats of consequential, physically plausible local records can distinguish stable associations from variable labels.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Reproducibility evidence can prevent single unusual labels from driving inappropriate corrections across many related rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m72's low-loading DCM-loaded 10/1 response and m81's middle-loading 20/1 completion dip reproduce?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes reject the proposed extension of m207's compact 5/1 region across loading: both 78 and 234 mg completions exceeded 34 mL, compared with 10.42 mL at 156 mg. Its 10/1 onset instead decreased smoothly with loading. I therefore test the scope of that irregularity at 2/1 and use m135's surrounding 5/1 masses to assess whether the other benzylic alcohol has a stable transition. The m135 2/1 bridge measured 10.43/16.54 mL, placing its larger increase later along the curve. m194's middle-loading 2/1 completion matched the upper-loading value rather than interpolating between the extremes; its 1/1 loading comparison now becomes more informative. The acid's 10/1 completions were nearly unchanged across the two measured masses, limiting the large loading association seen at 20/1. Its new 50/1 record, 0.133/-0.100 mL, is physically inconsistent with the endpoint definitions and cannot support a genuine retention-collapse hypothesis. The latest m40 50/1 measurement revealed a large acquisition-time underprediction, while its 10/1 label and the tetralone bridge were much closer to predictions. This shifts carbonyl follow-up toward transition localization and selective structural boundaries. The m87 measurements established a local completion decrease, but the predicted decreases in m117, m99, branched acrylate and the alkyne diester disappeared. I reduce emphasis on those resolved shape checks and test transfer of the measured m87 decrease alongside uncovered endpoint-order warnings. Finally, the m92 EA-loaded 1/1 repeat reproduced its low completion, whereas both m9 loading-solvent comparisons were small. This strengthens the local glyoxylate association and weakens any global solvent-offset explanation. All numerical errors discussed are acquisition-time errors; current candidate predictions remain unmeasured.
batch_rationale: The batch covers 19 scaffolds, with repeated molecules serving explicit comparisons. The alcohol, ether-aldehyde, acid and thiol-ester experiments constrain where loading associations apply and which endpoint they affect. The m40 bridges and higher-loading weak-eluent point repair the scope of a recent large miss, while m68, p-iodoacetophenone and the dialdehyde test structural transfer boundaries. The m87 pair asks whether an observed reversal generalizes across mass; m53, prenyl bromide and the boronate address uncovered response shapes and endpoint-order warnings. Two exact-condition repeats assess consequential local constraints even though their condition novelty and CW distance are low. Glyoxylate measurements extend a reproduced condition association into a loading-by-eluent comparison, and the two pure-EA nitrogen-scaffold points explore stronger-eluent boundaries with measured same-loading references. These labels can improve Row-distribution generalization by locating transitions, distinguishing endpoint-specific interactions and limiting overextension of corrections. CW distance is supplementary coverage evidence, and single-predictor quantile spans are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. V2 minus V1 remains the elution interval. Loading mass is the supplied density-times-volume feature, and missing experimental factors limit causal interpretation. The exact supplied predictions associated with the selected IDs are frozen before any new label reveal.
